subject: Dedicated capacity commitment variants for Zenith Labs - options and timelines
messages:
From: Alice Park <alice@zenithlabs.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@zenithlabs.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity — short POC + production ramp (numbers attached)

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team was impressed with the latency and the burst behavior you showed. We're starting to scope a short POC (2–3 weeks) that could flip to production for one of our customer-facing features. Before we lock timelines, procurement asked for a clear set of reserved-capacity options we can share with execs.

Quick background: expected seeds for the initial POC are about 500 concurrent users, moving to ~10k monthly active users in month 3 post-launch. We've attached a simple forecast (zenith_MAU_forecast.xlsx) for reference.

Can you send a short options matrix for dedicated reservations — cluster size, minimum GPU commitment, typical activation lead time, and a conservative ramp schedule? Also include any recommended guardrails for latency SLOs and fallback model variants.

Looking to present to our CTO on Monday.

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Park
Head of Platform Engineering, Zenith Labs

Attachment: zenith_MAU_forecast.xlsx (xlsx)

From: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Alice Park <alice@zenithlabs.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — short POC + production ramp (numbers attached)

Hi Alice — thanks for the forecast, that's helpful. Attached is a concise options matrix (Redwood_Dedicated_Options_v1.pdf) with three commitment variants and the expected activation/ramp timelines. TL;DR below — full details in the attached.

- Variant A — Fleet Flex (minimal reserve):
  - Cluster size: shared 8-GPU lane (pooled across customers)
  - Minimum committed GPUs: 0 (burst capable), soft priority on capacity
  - Typical lead time: immediate (within 48 hours) for POC lanes
  - Ramp: no reservation; recommend prefix cache for POC to reduce cost
  - Use case: short POCs, variable traffic; lower up-front cost

- Variant B — Staged Reserve (recommended for lean production):
  - Cluster size: 8–16 GPUs dedicated (NVIDIA H100 equivalent)
  - Minimum committed GPUs: 8 (monthly contract)
  - Typical lead time: 10–14 days for dedicated pool activation
  - Ramp schedule: Month 0: 8 GPUs (POC staging), Month 1: 8–12 (can burst), Month 3: 16 (full production)
  - Use case: predictable throughput with room to burst; balanced cost/latency

- Variant C — Performance Reserve (throughput-first):
  - Cluster size: 32–48 GPUs dedicated (multi-node cluster)
  - Minimum committed GPUs: 32
  - Typical lead time: 4–6 weeks for scheduled capacity + networking
  - Ramp schedule: Stage 1 (2 weeks test): 16 GPUs, Stage 2 (go-live): 32 GPUs, Stage 3 (3mo): 48 GPUs if MAU growth meets forecast
  - Use case: enterprise SLA, stable peak load, lowest tail latency

Notes on SLOs and fallbacks:
- We recommend targeting 99th percentile generation latency <= 500ms for short prompts on Staged Reserve; Performance Reserve can target <250ms depending on model choice and quantization.
- Fallback policy: automatic routing to smaller quantized variants in case of capacity pressure; prefix KV cache to preserve tokens and reduce cost.

I'll loop Ben for the exact kernel/gpu recommendations and Laura for billing/contract cadence. If you have a target activation date for production, we can propose a Mutual Action Plan.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redwood_Dedicated_Options_v1.pdf (pdf)

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alice Park <alice@zenithlabs.com>, tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 13:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — short POC + production ramp (numbers attached)

Hi Alice / Tessa — quick technical notes from infra to help choose between B/C:

- GPU spec: For low-latency generation at the volumes you describe, we recommend H100 80GB or an equivalent 8-bit quantized A100 profile if latency constraints are relaxed.
- Concurrency & lanes: 8 GPUs will comfortably handle ~250 concurrent short-text generations (<= 256 tokens) with batching. Expect sustained throughput improvements once KV cache warms.
- Autoscale buffer: plan for a 20–30% burst buffer for peak days; Redwood Dedicated supports burst lanes that kick in automatically but count against burst credits in Variant B.
- Ramp testing: we suggest a 14-day soak at each stage with synthetic load plus a real-user canary (10% traffic).

Operational caveats: if you need guaranteed single-region residency with private networking, add 7–10 days to lead time. Also flag any regulatory data retention needs now (logs, KV retention).

I'll coordinate with our provisioning team to validate node counts and cross-check price estimates.

-ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Zenith Labs Procurement <procure@zenithlabs.com>

Cc: Alice Park <alice@zenithlabs.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 10:09:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — short POC + production ramp (numbers attached)

Tessa — procurement questions below (we'll need answers to share with legal/finance):

1) SLA credits and remedies if SLOs missed for Performance Reserve.
2) Early termination / scale-down options after month 6.
3) Activation lead time guarantees and any associated fees.
4) Data handling: can you confirm logs/audit retention windows and deletion timelines for private deployments?

Also, can you confirm whether the 8 GPU minimum in Variant B is billed pro-rata from activation date or full-month?

Thanks — Rajiv (on behalf of procurement).

--
Zenith Labs Procurement

From: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Zenith Labs Procurement <procure@zenithlabs.com>, Alice Park <alice@zenithlabs.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — short POC + production ramp (numbers attached)

Hi Rajiv / team — answers inline and next steps: 

1) SLA credits: Performance Reserve includes a 99.9% uptime SLO with a tiered credit schedule (5% credit for single-week miss, escalates). We'll send the SLA appendix as part of the term sheet.

2) Scale-downs & early termination: Standard commitments are month-to-month after a 90-day minimum term for Variant B; Variant C has a 6-month minimum with pro-rata options for scale-downs at 30 days' notice. We'll reflect these in the contract.

3) Activation lead time: Variant B (8 GPU) — target 10–14 days after PO; Variant C (32 GPU) — 4–6 weeks. We can offer a 48–72 hour POC lane for immediate testing at no additional fee. There is a one-time activation fee for dedicated networking ($X, to be included in final quote).

4) Data handling: logs and audit trails retained for 90 days by default; can extend to 1 year for an additional compliance package. For private deployments, we support customer-managed KMS and data deletion on contract end; we'll include the deletion workflow.

Mutual Action Plan (proposed):
- Week 0: Sign PO / finalize terms (T+3 business days)
- Week 1: POC lane activation (48–72h) + canonical test set run (Ben)
- Weeks 2–3: Staged Reserve activation (8 GPUs) + canary (10% traffic)
- Month 1–3: Ramp per Variant B schedule; review checkpoints at Month 1 and Month 3
- Month 3+: Evaluate need for upgrade to Variant C

Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_Options_v1_revA.pdf (includes SLA appendix and activation fees).

Links: HubSpot plan: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/zenith/record/ZD-2027-0414 and DocuSign term sheet: https://www.docusign.com/links/zenith-dedicated-term-sheet

If this looks good we'll convert the PO and target a mid-May go-live window.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
